PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT Deputy City Attorney Gloria Ramirez delivered a report on the Closed Session matters as follows:

Item #1.A to 1.C: The City Negotiator, City Manager Cisneros, provided a comprehensive briefing. Subsequently, the City Council took necessary action, which will be duly documented during the upcoming regular City Council meeting as items #6 through #9.

Item #2: There were no discussions held on this particular item.

Item #3.A and 3.B: A thorough briefing was presented, and the City Council provided specific guidance. However, no action that requires formal reporting was taken on these items.

PUBLIC COMMENT Gloria Nezahualcoyatl expressed her opposition to an increase in City Council compensation and the revision of benefits. She also raised concerns about the vehicle allowance and suggested redirecting those funds towards parks and recreation programs.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia expressed her appreciation for the thoughtful gift of flowers. She also commended the Parks and Recreation professionals for their remarkable efforts in bringing the community together and creating a positive impact. She attended a 4th of July celebration and was thoroughly impressed by the performances. Notably, she celebrated the recognition of two outstanding athletes, Hall of Champions Roy Amos (Wrestler) and Sandy Nitta (Water Polo), and participated in the unveiling of a plaque honoring the first generation of female water polo athletes who inspired the local sports community. Additionally, Councilmember Garcia attended the NALEO conference, which she found to be a fantastic opportunity for professional development.

Councilmember Lainez, too, expressed gratitude for the flowers and praised the Parks and Recreation department for their continuous efforts in organizing various events. He attended several notable occasions, including the Robert Garcia Open House in Long Beach, the Independence Day celebration, and the induction ceremony of two Hall of Champions athletes, along with the unveiling of a plaque honoring women in Water Polo. He also attended the impressive Unplugged Theatre Showcase Cabaret, appreciating the exceptional talent on display. Furthermore, Councilmember Lainez mentioned having met with Senator Lena Gonzalez, who would soon be representing the City of Commerce as a State representative, and also attended the NALEO conference.

Vice Mayor Altamirano extended his thanks to the Parks and Recreation team for their dedicated work. He joined in celebrating the 4th of July event and expressed admiration for Councilmember Garcia's initiative to remember pioneering young women in water polo and their Olympic endeavors. He also expressed gratitude to the residents and colleagues who supported him during challenging times when his parents underwent surgery. Vice Mayor Altamirano also attended the NALEO event.

Mayor Argumedo echoed the sentiments of appreciation for the 4th of July celebration and thanked Councilmember Garcia for her efforts in recognizing the achievements of past female athletes. He attended the district office of Robert Garcia's Open House in Long Beach and had the opportunity to meet Lena Gonzalez, who would be representing the City after her reelection. The Mayor found the NALEO conference to be a valuable networking experience.

ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:15 in memory of Angela Carbajal, City employee.
